objects.title: Architecture decision integrity
objects.description: Every architecture decision the repository holds parses against the decision contract, claims an identity nothing else claims, and every relation and reference it makes resolves.

objects.title: AI layer integrity
objects.description: The repository's AI layer is real: the manifest declares a format this executable reads and every section it names exists, the checkout-local half is ignored by git and nothing under it is tracked, and no project data remains under the pre-.ai .majordomus/ path.

objects.title: Blocker resolution
objects.description: No task can be completed while any question on this branch is unresolved; it can still be finished as blocked, partial, no_match or failed.

objects.title: Bootstrap integrity
objects.description: The path from a human reader to the AI layer is unbroken — README.md names AGENTS.md, every generated instruction file points at .ai/README.md, and none of them carries a rule of its own.

objects.title: Candidates are reviewed
objects.description: A review queue that grows without bound is not reviewed. More candidates than the policy cap, a candidate that has waited longer than the policy age, or a candidate the tree does not track, is reported, not stopped; both numbers are declared once in the policy.

objects.title: Catalogue integrity
objects.description: Every use case and application describes the tool in terms the tool has — each command, doctrine and claim it names exists, and the two catalogues reference each other in both directions.

objects.title: Checkpoint freshness
objects.description: A task whose last checkpoint is older than its profile's interval is reported, not stopped.

objects.title: Every public command is exercised and refuted
objects.description: Every public command has a behavioural test and a negative test, computed from the registry and the coverage each case declares about itself rather than from a list someone maintains.

objects.title: The command surface is declared and reconciled
objects.description: Every command the binary dispatches is described by the shipped registry, every command the registry declares public is dispatched, and a command is public exactly when the usage text lists it.

objects.title: Completion is gated
objects.description: A task reaches the outcome completed only when no validation gate its own change set selects is known to be failing, and a gate's verdict discharges nothing once the files that select it have changed since the run.

objects.title: Context budget
objects.description: The always-loaded projection stays within its line budget, every reference in it resolves, it states no count that will go stale, and the assembled context fits the builder's own budget.

objects.title: Context integrity
objects.description: Every directory of the AI layer carries a context document, each one carries the contract, they compose into one deterministic chain for every path, and a tree that does not validate resolves nothing.

objects.title: Dependency graph integrity
objects.description: The issue dependency graph is acyclic, every edge names an issue that exists, and no issue is executing ahead of a dependency that is not done.

objects.title: Decision records
objects.description: Every entry in decisions.md carries the task, the head and the reason, so a decision can be found by the worker who needs it.

objects.title: The decision threshold
objects.description: A change that is hard to reverse records the decision behind it as a decision record, and names what it put in force; an ordinary change does not.

objects.title: Define done before executing
objects.description: The finish contract is evaluated line by line, and nothing else counts as done.

objects.title: A deployment is described once, and every artifact built from it is generated from it
objects.description: A deployment of the executable is a canonical object of the layer against a closed contract; the container definition, its ignore file and the files of the provider it names are projections of it, never a second description.

objects.title: Execution depth is not output verbosity
objects.description: Think as hard as the task needs; report as briefly as the profile says.

objects.title: Doctrine wiring integrity
objects.description: Every doctrine in this registry resolves to a validator that exists, is reached from every command it names, propagates failure, is proved by a test, and is run by CI — and every validator in the source is declared here.

objects.title: Enforcement wiring
objects.description: Every enforcement the policy declares is invoked by the hook it names, from a file the dispatcher will actually execute, without swallowing the exit code.

objects.title: Externalise decisions and durable state
objects.description: A decision you make goes into a record, dated, with what was rejected and why; a question for a person goes into the questions store.

objects.title: Handover integrity
objects.description: The resolver runs and reports either the record for this worktree and branch or its clean absence; a malformed record is never silently skipped, and a record describing a history this checkout no longer has is reported.

objects.title: Handovers transfer state, not transcripts
objects.description: A handover says what is true now and the one next action; never conversation history.

objects.title: Parallel work requires isolation
objects.description: Do not start a second task in a checkout that already has one; overlapping claims across worktrees are reported.

objects.title: Escalate capability and effort only when justified
objects.description: The profile sets the default capability and effort; escalation is recorded, never assumed.

objects.title: Knowledge graph integrity
objects.description: The graph the knowledge compiler builds from what the repository states has one node per identity, no edge with a missing end or without provenance, and no declared path or tracked source that no longer exists; a broken owned reference is a failure, a broken link an author wrote in prose is not.

objects.title: Knowledge integrity
objects.description: Every knowledge record is one evidenced, well-formed assertion. It is valid against its schema with no unknown key, its identity is unique and equals its file name, a verified record carries provenance, every reference it names resolves, a superseded record says what replaced it or why it was rejected, a candidate never claims to be verified, and no record carries a conversation.

objects.title: Knowledge observation
objects.description: While episodes keep closing, the knowledge they produced must keep being derived. A closed episode no derivation followed, once it is older than the freshness threshold, is a stopped writer; a lifecycle whose close path never calls the deriver while the policy switch is on is a writer that was never started.

objects.title: Layout integrity
objects.description: The directories the durable commands write into are installed rather than created on first use.

objects.title: Ledger integrity
objects.description: Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event; the one durable record nothing else can reconstruct stays readable.

objects.title: Lifecycle observation
objects.description: A store that can be read is not a store that is being written. While episodes go on opening, the records a future worker resumes from must go on advancing, every lifecycle event received must leave evidence it arrived, and an episode that outlives the staleness threshold must be named rather than left open.

objects.title: Load minimum sufficient context
objects.description: The profile says what to load; discover everything that may apply and load only what does.

objects.title: Note integrity
objects.description: Every outcome needs a note carrying the sections that outcome requires, and no transcript.

objects.title: Obligation closure
objects.description: A task that declares obligations reaches the outcome completed only when each one is established by the tool or has evidence, and that evidence still describes the tree or the commit it was taken over.

objects.title: One worker, one clear scope
objects.description: A task claims the paths it may touch, and touches only those.

objects.title: Policy completeness
objects.description: Every policy value the code reads is declared in the skeleton policy, and no reader carries its own default for one.

objects.title: Policy integrity
objects.description: The policy and every profile parse, declare version 1, and carry no key the schema does not define.

objects.title: Profile requirements
objects.description: A profile may demand more than the shared contract — a regression test, a decision record — and finish refuses without it.

objects.title: Project model integrity
objects.description: Every milestone and issue file parses, carries the id its filename claims, and contains no key nobody reads.

objects.title: Projection integrity
objects.description: Every generated instruction file exists, matches the stamp it carries, and is never silently overwritten after a hand edit.

objects.title: Prompt capture is proven, or reported unavailable
objects.description: A repository that declares prompt capture has it wired below the model and proven by running it; the archive stays ignored and untracked, every prompt is present as both a record and a rendering, and neither carries anything the model said.

objects.title: A prompt record carries its own identity, is bounded, and is private
objects.description: Every captured prompt names the episode it belongs to or says why it cannot; the archive is readable by its owner alone, bounded by a declared retention policy, and never holds credential material verbatim.

objects.title: Prompt integrity
objects.description: Every repository-local prompt asset renders, and every token in it is one the renderer knows.

objects.title: A session does not finish behind its own published site
objects.description: A repository that publishes has a second tree — the one the public is being served — and no commit-level gate can measure it, because no change to any file can make it right or wrong. A session that lands work and leaves the publication owed has finished nothing the public can see, and every check stays green while that is true. The gates that measure a deployment are declared as such in the CI model, and finish asks them.

objects.title: Questions store integrity
objects.description: Every entry in open-questions.md parses, because a gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one.

objects.title: A record's changed_files names the work, not the tool's exhaust
objects.description: The changed_files block of a checkpoint, a handover or a closed session names what the episode produced. Paths a declaration already calls generated, projected or local are classified out, and the classification reads those declarations rather than a list of its own.

objects.title: Retention caps
objects.description: The ledger, the handovers, the checkpoints and the session records stay under the caps the policy sets, so durable state does not grow without bound.

objects.title: The roadmap is a projection, never a document
objects.description: No document is a second authority for the roadmap, and no milestone types its own version. While a hand-written roadmap table exists, it can neither list a release no milestone was released in nor hide one that carried a milestone; a milestone's release (released_in) is inferred from the release records, never typed.

objects.title: Rule package integrity
objects.description: The repository's effective rule set is real: the vendored baseline matches its manifest file for file, every rule resolves with its dependencies and no two claim one identity, and no project rule reuses the vendored namespace.

objects.title: Every object has a schema, and the rules resolve in one stated order
objects.description: The order the rules apply in is written down rather than left in the code; every kind the tool reads declares a schema, every schema is named by a kind, and every path under the repository's AI layer is claimed by a source so that nothing is carried through unvalidated.

objects.title: Scope integrity
objects.description: A task touches only the paths it claimed; work found elsewhere is not accepted as done.

objects.title: The episode boundary is drawn below the model, and its working context is local
objects.description: Where a provider fires session events, the episode is opened and closed by that provider's hook rather than by the model, the start event hands the worker the bounded briefing the policy declares, and the working context each open freezes stays under the ignored half of the layer, carries the declared keys, and never carries a conversation.

objects.title: Session records are shared objects with a closed field set
objects.description: A closed execution episode is written once, into the layer's sessions section, against a schema that admits what the repository can prove and nothing else.

objects.title: Sessions are workers, not memory
objects.description: Durable state lives in records the repository keeps, never in a conversation.

objects.title: Skill integrity
objects.description: Every skill the repository declares parses against the skill contract, names the directory it lives in, carries its sections, describes itself in terms no other skill uses, and every skill or example it refers to exists.

objects.title: State consistency
objects.description: The task record still describes this checkout — same branch, and HEAD at or ahead of the recorded commit.

objects.title: Task continuity
objects.description: A task finished as partial or blocked should leave a handover record, not only a note section.

objects.title: A task on a repository whose mesh is enabled works on the mesh
objects.description: When the repository declares its mesh enabled, an active task's scope is claimed on the mesh — `start` brings the checkout's shared server up and claims it, `check` and `finish` claim it again when a server answers — and a task completed without that claim is refused.

objects.title: Use-case coverage
objects.description: Every public command, and every guaranteed claim and MCP tool the policy asks for, is named and run by at least one active use case whose scenario executes against the real tool; a gap is a failure or a report according to the policy, never silence.

objects.title: Verification integrity
objects.description: Completion requires a verification command that actually ran and exited 0 over a tree that did not change under it; its exit code, duration and tree are recorded.

objects.title: Verify outcomes, not activity
objects.description: A test that ran and passed is evidence; a sentence saying it did is not.

objects.title: Every client engagement with measurable sources has its own anonymised, derived case study; every figure says how it is known
objects.description: scripts/build-cases.mjs writes one page per engagement of data/experience.json that has a sector and inferred capabilities, in every language, linked to its skills, services, technologies and public twins; the sector and roles are declared, the period and scale measured and rounded, the capabilities inferred and labelled so; no client, person, system or repository of an engagement is named.

objects.title: Every number on the site is measured, dated and derived
objects.description: Figures come from data/github.json written by scripts/fetch-github.mjs and are shown with their date; the curated catalogue is data/projects.toml; llms.txt is derived and checked.

objects.title: Repository dossiers are inferred, carry their provenance and say so wherever shown
objects.description: data/dossiers/<repo>.json holds, for each original public repository, a problem, a solution, a stack and a Mermaid architecture inferred from the repository's own files; each carries the commit and date it was read at and a confidence, is labelled inferred wherever it is shown, is re-mined when the repository's head moves, and passes the NDA gate.

objects.title: Every original repository on GitHub and GitLab has its own complete page, derived and gated
objects.description: The original repositories of data/index.json (both forges, merged) are the one set; each has a work page in every language with a title, description, SEO title, Open Graph card, canonical, hreflang and SoftwareSourceCode JSON-LD derived from measured facts, recent ones dated by period and the rest as honestly dated archive; the scheduled refresh re-derives them and a gate fails on any repository without a page or a page that is not complete.

objects.title: Everything links to everything it names, through derived links that are proven
objects.description: Every mark a visual draws, every term, language, technology, project, category and repository a page names leads to its page on this site (and to its source where there is none), in the page's language; links come from one derived index, never from addresses built by hand, and every link is resolved at build time and in the browser audit.

objects.title: Pages are front matter plus data; nothing is maintained by hand, and no SEO field types a count
objects.description: Every page is described by front matter that matches static/schemas/front-matter.schema.json, everything else is derived from data that the scheduled refresh re-measures, the whole site is published as data (site.json, llms.txt), and the search and social fields of the front matter carry no typed count.

objects.title: One positioning from cv.hire.headline on every surface, every page links /hire/, nothing hidden
objects.description: While data/cv.toml [hire] says the owner is available, the name and the headline lead the home h1, the titles, the profile OG cards, the JSON-LD jobTitle, llms.txt and resume.json, every page links /hire/ from its navigation, and every hire fact is visible text first; available = false removes every signal with no other edit.

objects.title: Every text exists in every language, through Zola's multilingual features
objects.description: Interface texts live in i18n/*.toml, grouped by feature, and reach templates through trans(); curated data carries a _cs twin for every text field; every page exists as x.md and x.cs.md; tags are Zola taxonomies; a gate fails on anything untranslated.

objects.title: The landing's chapters, their ids and order are a contract; every element links, every figure is measured, nothing is hidden
objects.description: The home page answers a hiring team in ten seconds and an engineer in ten minutes in fixed chapters with stable ids; every element in its main region leads to its page, every figure comes from data/ or Zola, owner facts only from data/cv.toml, ?role= only reorders and labels, at most four mail links, nothing hidden, and no inflated label.

objects.title: No client, person or private source is ever named in this public repository
objects.description: Work done under a non-disclosure agreement reaches the site only as anonymised, mined facts; no client or person name, private repository, path or copied text appears in any tracked file, built page or commit message, and the gate that checks it reads its list from outside the repository.

objects.title: Every count in running text agrees with its word, in every language and at every number the data can give
objects.description: A text with a count either takes the plural form its number needs (key__one, key__few, key__other, chosen by scripts/lib/derive.mjs t() in generators and by the count component in templates) or is phrased so that no form depends on the number ("Pages: {n}", "in commits ({n})"); scripts/check-numerals.mjs refuses a disagreeing count anywhere in the built site.

objects.title: Every page is also an educational, linked article, described in front matter
objects.description: Every content page carries a Markdown article body and names the glossary terms it builds on (extra.terms); the glossary (data/glossary.toml) defines each term in both languages with a source; term pages and back-links are derived; a gate refuses a page without an article or terms, an unknown term, an unused term or an unchecked link.

objects.title: Search and social metadata are derived from front matter and data, and state only what the page shows
objects.description: Titles, descriptions, canonical URLs, Open Graph and Twitter tags, OG images and JSON-LD come from each page's front matter and data/, through templates/partials/seo.html and scripts/build-og.mjs; structured data states only what the page visibly shows, OG cards caption the page's own permalink, and all of it is gated on the built site.

objects.title: Services, skills, knowledge and domains form one derived, interlinked model; only the words are written
objects.description: Every service (data/services.toml) and every skill (a capability of data/experience-rules.toml) has its own page in every language; the owner writes only their words, while the skills a service draws on, the technologies, the public evidence, the client use cases (sector and role only) and the articles are derived by scripts/lib/services.mjs, and every skill links its concept (a glossary term), its domain, its services and its evidence.

objects.title: The site is Zola, self-hosted, and deployed only by the Pages workflow
objects.description: Zola 0.23 (Tera 2) builds the site from templates and data; every asset is self-hosted; master deploys through pages.yml after CI, and production is verified to serve the commit.

objects.title: Every language and technology has its own page with derived evidence; every project page embeds its live README
objects.description: Each language and technology the measured data names (repositories' languages, curated stacks, the technologies the repository dossiers find, the mined engagements' technologies) has a glossary term whose page shows the evidence derived from the data (repositories, how each uses it, what it solves, years, categories, live sites, a reference graph) and the client use cases without names, dates or numbers; each work page renders its repository's README live from the forge instead of copying it.

objects.title: A UI change passes the browser gate before it lands
objects.description: Every page, at phone and desktop width in both themes, has no WCAG 2.2 AA violation, no console or network error, no horizontal overflow, CLS at most 0.1, every visual mounted, and every internal link resolving.

objects.title: Every page is built on Flowbite Pro
objects.description: The site is the owner's licensed Flowbite Pro application shell and blocks on Tailwind 4 and the flowbite 4 plugin; no other kit, no Pro source file committed.

objects.title: Every visual goes through one component layer
objects.description: p5.js, D3 and Apache ECharts are constructed only in static/js/viz/<name>.js, registered with KorczisHub.viz, lazy-loaded, themed from the CSS tokens and given a text alternative.

objects.title: Every visual is a maximizable simulator on the best library
objects.description: Every visual that is not declared static can be maximized to the viewport, deep-linked, restored with Escape, and is a model the visitor drives through declared parameters whose state lives in the address; charts and graphs are Apache ECharts through the layer, D3 is for bespoke layouts and physics, p5 for generative art.

objects.title: Build UI on Flowbite Pro
objects.description: Build or change any user interface on the owner's licensed Flowbite Pro shell, blocks and components, and verify it before claiming compliance.

objects.title: Getting started and adoption
objects.description: Bringing the tool into a repository, new or old, without losing what people already wrote.

objects.title: Completion and quality gates
objects.description: Deciding whether work is finished, with a contract every line of which passes or fails.

objects.title: Sessions and handover
objects.description: Stopping and resuming work across sessions and workers from durable state.

objects.title: Drift and reconciliation
objects.description: Detecting that policy, projections, state and git disagree, and putting them back in step.

objects.title: Extension
objects.description: Adding a rule, a command or a use case as data, with the checks that follow from it.

objects.title: Repository knowledge
objects.description: What the repository declares about itself, and the plan, searched and validated.

objects.title: Policy and enforcement
objects.description: Declaring rules, proving they are wired, reproducing a finding.

objects.title: Parallel workers
objects.description: Several agents or people on one repository: claimed scopes, overlap, who touched what.
